chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed Ibn Uqdah, who reported from Muhammad ibn Haroon ibn Abdul Rahman al-Hijazi, who reported from his father, who reported from Isa ibn Abil Ward, from Ahmad ibn Abdul Aziz, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said:
Amirul Mu'mineen Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, said: "No deed is little when accompanied by Taqwa (God-consciousness). And how can that which is accepted (by Allah) be little?!"

key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa — God-consciousness, piety, and mindfulness of Allah in all actions
key_terms.عمل: deed, action — any act of worship or good conduct
key_terms.يتقبل: is accepted — divine acceptance of a deed, which is conditional on sincerity and Taqwa

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about deeds performed with Taqwa (God-consciousness)?
ai.summary: Imam Ali teaches that any deed, no matter how small, becomes significant when performed with Taqwa (God-consciousness and piety). The rhetorical question emphasizes that since Allah accepts deeds done with sincere piety, they can never be considered insignificant. This saying highlights that the quality and sincerity of worship matters more than its outward quantity.
